title: app-gateway settings
description: Settings for the gateway itself. No app appears here — an app is a file in apps/, described by app.schema.json.

bind.description: Public listen address for the one Caddy the gateway runs. This is the address the tunnel forwards to, so it should rarely change; -Bind overrides it for a single run.

site.description: Chrome for the generated landing page. Present so no app-specific text is baked into the builder.

fallbackIcon.description: Card icon for an app that declares none.

paths.description: Named directories, referenced as ${paths.NAME} in an app's root. Relative values resolve against this file's directory. They exist so relocating a checkout is one edit here rather than one per app.

runtime.description: Where the generated Caddyfile and landing page are written, relative to this file. Both are rewritten on every launch; nothing else in the folder is touched.

logs.description: Folder for logs/<app>.log (every child's output, rotated to .1 past 5 MB when a run first writes it) and admin-audit.log. Disposable logs; registry backups live separately under backups. Relative to this file.

backups.description: Persistent folder for previous and deleted app registrations saved by the admin page (Config -> History). Kept separate from logs so clearing logs never discards recovery history. Relative to this file.

caddyAdmin.description: Caddy's admin endpoint, through which the admin page hands it new routes without a restart. In the gateway's own slot of playround/PORTS.md rather than Caddy's default 2019, which any second Caddy on the box would also want. Loopback only: anything that can reach it can reconfigure Caddy.

admin.description: The admin page at /admin/, served by start.ps1 itself. It can start, stop and restart apps, follow their logs, edit the registry and reload Caddy's routes, so it sits behind a sign-in.

enabled.description: -NoAdmin turns it off for one run.

port.description: localhost port the page listens on, behind Caddy. In the gateway's slot of playround/PORTS.md.

sessionHours.description: Idle time after which a session is signed out. A session lasts at most seven days, and none survives a restart of the gateway.

ports.description: The port convention the gateway follows, relative to this file. Its Ranges table gives each directory's range and the slot size; every app whose root lies under a ranged directory must declare its ports inside that range, in one slot or in consecutive slots when it needs more than one. Checked at launch, after -Port, so an override cannot leave the app's own slots either. An app under no ranged directory is not checked.
